title: Run KMC simulations with and without incorporation
action: Implement a solid-on-solid kinetic Monte Carlo model on a 300×300 periodic lattice at T=560 K with attempt frequency ν0=10^12 s⁻¹, diffusion barrier E_B=0.9 eV, nearest-neighbour bond energy E_N=0.25 eV, and Ehrlich-Schwoebel barrier E_S=0.1 eV. Deposition rate F=1 ML/s. For the with-incorporation variant, after each deposition event allow the particle to instantly relax to any lower neighbour within one lattice constant. Run both variants (with and without incorporation) for 1000 ML of deposition. Record the full surface height array at regular intervals (e.g., every 10 ML) into separate files for later analysis.
description: The core KMC simulation that generates the raw height configurations – required to produce the surface width time series.

title: Compute surface width without incorporation
action: From the recorded height data of the simulation without incorporation, for every recorded time (every 10 ML), compute the root-mean-square surface width w(t) = sqrt(⟨(h_i − ⟨h⟩)²⟩). Write a CSV file with columns 'time' (in ML) and 'surface_width' (in lattice units).
description: Time series of surface width for the KMC simulation without the incorporation rule.
output_schema: Two columns: time (float, units ML), surface_width (float, units lattice constants). Times are strictly increasing.

title: Compute surface width with incorporation
action: From the recorded height data of the simulation with incorporation, compute the surface width at each recorded time and write a CSV file in the same format as the without-incorporation file.
description: Time series of surface width for the KMC simulation with the incorporation rule.
output_schema: Two columns: time (float, units ML), surface_width (float, units lattice constants). Times are strictly increasing.
